text.p: These are the leading stories in Zambia's newspapers on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Transport and communications minister Paul Kapinga and commissioner for refugees in the ministry of home affairs, Lameck Mwaba, die from unrelated causes.

- Finance minister Ronald Penza is found guilty of contempt of court over comments he made criticising a ruling by the industrial court that government increase public servants salaries by 45 percent.
- The opposition National Party, which boycotted general elections held last November, says it will contest forthcoming local government elections, but under protest.
- The southern border town of Livingstone is to be turned into a duty free zone, the ministry of commerce says.
- An association of independent news organisation sets up an independent media council to regulate journalism.
